column1: In SQL Server, what is a common table expression (CTE)?
column2:
A named result set defined by a query.
The statement that follows can reference the CTE by name.
Review source

column1: How many following statements can use one SQL Server CTE definition?
column2:
One statement.
A later statement needs its own CTE definition.
Review source

column1: What is a minimal SQL Server CTE that returns the number 1?
column2:
WITH N AS (SELECT 1 AS n) SELECT n FROM N;
AS introduces the query inside parentheses.
Review source

column1: What must terminate a preceding statement before a SQL Server CTE in the same batch?
column2:
A semicolon.
Writing ;WITH also terminates an otherwise unterminated preceding statement.
Review source

column1: What separates multiple CTE definitions in one SQL Server WITH clause?
column2:
A comma.
Use WITH once and separate the named definitions with commas.
Review source

column1: Where must a different CTE appear before another CTE can reference it in the same SQL Server WITH clause?
column2:
Earlier in the WITH clause.
SQL Server does not allow forward references to later CTE definitions.
Review source

column1: How can one SQL Server query reference the same CTE in two join inputs?
column2:
Reference its name twice with different aliases.
The CTE needs only one definition for that statement.
Review source

column1: Why can repeated references to a SQL Server CTE repeat query work?
column2:
CTE results are not automatically stored for reuse.
A CTE definition does not guarantee that its query runs only once.
Review source

column1: Which type of SQL Server CTE references itself to traverse a hierarchy?
column2:
A recursive CTE.
Employee-manager relationships are a common example.
Review source

column1: Which member supplies the initial rows of a recursive SQL Server CTE?
column2:
The anchor member.
It runs before the recursive member.
Review source

column1: In a recursive SQL Server CTE, which rows feed the next recursive iteration?
column2:
The rows returned by the immediately preceding iteration.
The recursive member builds the next level from those rows.
Review source

column1: Which operator must connect the last anchor member to the first recursive member in SQL Server?
column2:
UNION ALL.
UNION ALL preserves duplicate rows rather than removing them.
Review source

column1: What normally ends recursion in a SQL Server CTE?
column2:
The recursive member returns no rows.
Its filtering or join condition must eventually produce an empty result.
Review source

column1: What is SQL Server's default recursion limit for a recursive CTE?
column2:
100 recursion levels.
A MAXRECURSION hint can override the default for one statement.
Review source

column1: Which query hint limits a SQL Server recursive CTE to 200 recursion levels?
column2:
OPTION (MAXRECURSION 200)
The limit is a safeguard against excessive recursion.
Review source

column1: What does OPTION (MAXRECURSION 0) mean in SQL Server?
column2:
No recursion limit.
A faulty termination condition can then cause an infinite loop.
Review source

column1: Where does OPTION (MAXRECURSION n) belong in a SQL Server SELECT that uses a recursive CTE?
column2:
On the outermost SELECT statement.
Do not place OPTION inside the CTE definition.
Review source

column1: In a recursive date CTE, what expression advances DateValue by one day?
column2:
DATEADD(DAY, 1, DateValue)
The recursive member also needs a condition that stops at the intended end date.
Review source

column1: Which join retains generated dates from a CTE when no matching order exists?
column2:
LEFT JOIN.
Place the generated dates on the left side of the join.
Review source

column1: How does a CTE help an UPDATE choose which rows to change?
column2:
It defines target rows that the UPDATE references.
The CTE separates row-selection logic from the update operation.
Review source
